name: aisc360-22/lap
about: The rules of a lap, as the first run asked for them: the types and the grid of the deck as it shipped until 2026-11-11, which rules_a.json keeps, over the 18 rows of that deck. A type is as that deck had it, with a range for each quantity. The ranges are where the acceptance check samples parts, and are not limits of the standard.

types.what: a flat steel plate that a joint connects

fields.name: width
fields.what: its gross width, across the force it carries

fields.name: Fy
fields.what: the specified minimum yield stress of its steel

fields.name: Fu
fields.what: the specified minimum tensile strength of its steel

types.what: one line of two or more bolts in single shear through two plates, in a bearing-type joint that is pulled along the line

fields.name: fastener
fields.what: the strength group of the bolts, as Section J3.2 names it

fields.name: threads
fields.what: whether threads are in the shear plane

fields.name: diameter
fields.what: the nominal diameter of a bolt

fields.name: holes
fields.what: the type of the holes in both plates

fields.name: count
fields.what: the number of bolts in the line

fields.name: pitch
fields.what: the distance between the centres of neighbouring holes

fields.name: end
fields.what: the least distance from the centre of an end hole to the end of either plate, along the line

loads.name: pull
loads.what: the force the lap carries from one plate to the other along the line, as a required strength by LRFD load combinations

asks.what: whether the bolts must be pretensioned or the joint slip-critical
whether this type of hole may be used in this joint
minimum distance from an end hole to the end of a plate
minimum distance from a hole to the side edge of a plate
shear of the bolts with bearing and tearout at their holes
tension on the bolts together with shear
tensile rupture of each plate through its holes
shear of a plate as an element loaded in shear
block shear rupture of each plate
yielding and buckling of a plate in compression
bending of the plates, which a lap in single shear sets apart
